dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَا رِيم. كَيْفَ حَالُكِ الْيَوْم؟
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you, Reem. How are you today?

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. I'm a little tired.

dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.english: What happened to you?

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.english: I have a headache, and I can't sleep well.

dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.english: Do you have a fever?

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.arabic: لَا، لَكِنِّي أَشْعُرُ بِالدُّوَارِ. وَمَعِدَتِي تُؤْلِمُنِي.
dialogue.transliteration: laa, lakinnee ash3uru bid-duwaari. wa ma3idatee tu2limunee.
dialogue.english: No, but I feel dizzy. And my stomach hurts.

dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.english: It looks like you have a cold.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.english: Maybe. And you, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.arabic: بِخَيْر، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه. لَكِنِّي مُتْعَبٌ أَيْضًا.
dialogue.transliteration: bikhayr, al7amdu lillaah. lakinnee mut3abun aydan.
dialogue.english: Fine, thank God. But I'm tired too.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.english: Then we must rest.

dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.arabic: اِسْتَرِيحِي قَلِيلًا يَا رِيمُ، وَاشْرَبِي الْمَاء.
dialogue.transliteration: istareehee qaleelan yaa Reemu, washrabee al-maa2.
dialogue.english: Rest a little, Reem, and drink some water.

dialogue.speaker: Reem
dialogue.english: Thank you, Fahd.

pair.english: Looks like you have a cold.

lessons.culture: In Fusha, people answer كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ with بِخَيْر, الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه, even when they are not well, and then explain if asked. A sick person is wished سَلَامَتُكَ, and friends often advise rest and water.

exercises.prompt: A man asks you: 'كَيْفَ حَالُكَ الْيَوْم؟'. Say that you are fine, thank God.
exercises.tip: بِخَيْر is 'in goodness'; الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه gives thanks.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you: 'مَاذَا حَدَثَ لَكَ؟'. Say that you have a headache.
exercises.tip: عِنْدِي is 'I have'; the pain or illness follows.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: 'يَبْدُو أَنَّكَ مُصَابٌ بِالزُّكَام'. Agree with him.
exercises.tip: أَظُنُّ ذَلِك means 'I think so'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'عِنْدِي _____.' (I have a fever.)
exercises.tip: حُمَّى is 'fever'; حَرَارَة is 'temperature'.

exercises.prompt: A woman says: 'أَنَا _____.' (I'm tired.)
exercises.tip: A woman adds ة to the word: مُتْعَب becomes مُتْعَبَة.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I can't sleep well.'
exercises.tip: لَا before a present verb makes it negative.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'My stomach hurts.'
exercises.tip: أَلَمَ means 'to hurt'; the ending ـنِي means 'me'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Take some rest.' (to a man)
exercises.tip: To a woman the command ends in ي: اِسْتَرِيحِي.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks a woman how she is today?
exercises.tip: The ending كِ with a long ee sound is for a woman.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'I feel dizzy'?
exercises.tip: أَشْعُرُ بِ means 'I feel'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'جَيِّدًا / أَنَامُ / لَا'.
exercises.tip: The negative word comes first, then the verb.

dialogue.speaker: Saif
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ دَوَاءٌ لِلصُّدَاع؟
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. Do you have medicine for a headache?

dialogue.speaker: Lama
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Yes, here you are.

dialogue.speaker: Saif
dialogue.english: How much does this medicine cost?

dialogue.speaker: Lama
dialogue.english: Ten dinars.

dialogue.speaker: Saif
dialogue.english: Do I need a prescription?

dialogue.speaker: Lama
dialogue.arabic: لَا، لَيْسَ لِهَذَا الدَّوَاء. خُذْهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم.
dialogue.transliteration: laa, laysa lihaadhaa ad-dawaa2. khudhhu marratayni fee al-yawm.
dialogue.english: No, not for this medicine. Take it twice a day.

dialogue.speaker: Saif
dialogue.english: Before eating or after?

dialogue.speaker: Lama
dialogue.arabic: بَعْدَ الْأَكْل. وَهَذَا الدَّوَاءُ يُسَبِّبُ النُّعَاسَ قَلِيلًا.
dialogue.transliteration: ba3da al-akl. wa haadhaa ad-dawaa2u yusabbibu an-nu3aasa qaleelan.
dialogue.english: After eating. And this medicine makes you a bit sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Saif
dialogue.english: Alright. And I also want something for allergies.

dialogue.speaker: Lama
dialogue.arabic: عِنْدَنَا أَقْرَاصٌ جَيِّدَة. هَلْ تُرِيدُ لَاصِقَ جُرُوح؟
dialogue.transliteration: 3indanaa aqraasun jayyida. hal tureedu laasiqa juroo7?
dialogue.english: We have good pills. Do you want band-aids?

dialogue.speaker: Saif
dialogue.english: Yes, please. Thank you very much.

dialogue.speaker: Lama
dialogue.english: You're welcome. Get well soon.

pair.english: Do you have medicine for a headache?
How much does this medicine cost?

lessons.culture: A pharmacist in the Arab world often gives advice and sells many medicines without a prescription, and the word الصَّيْدَلِيَّة names the pharmacy. The polite farewell to a sick customer is سَلَامَتُكَ or شَفَاكَ اللَّه.

exercises.prompt: You are at the pharmacy. Ask whether they have medicine for a headache.
exercises.tip: هَلْ turns a statement into a yes or no question.

exercises.prompt: The pharmacist says: 'خُذْهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم'. Ask whether it is before eating or after.
exercises.tip: أَمْ is 'or' when choosing between two options.

exercises.prompt: A customer asks: 'هَلْ أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى وَصْفَةٍ طِبِّيَّة؟'. As the pharmacist, say no, not for this medicine.
exercises.tip: لَيْسَ negates the phrase that follows it.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أُرِيدُ _____ لِلْحُمَّى.' (I want pills for the fever.)
exercises.tip: قُرْص is one pill; أَقْرَاص is pills.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'خُذْهُ _____ فِي الْيَوْم.' (Take it twice a day.)
exercises.tip: مَرَّتَيْن is the dual of مَرَّة: exactly two times.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'How much does this medicine cost?'
exercises.tip: سِعْر is 'price'; كَمْ asks 'how much'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Do you have cough syrup?'
exercises.tip: شَرَاب is 'syrup' or 'drink'; سُعَال is 'cough'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'This medicine makes you a bit sleepy.'
exercises.tip: سَبَّبَ means 'to cause'; نُعَاس is 'sleepiness'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Do you have band-aids?'
exercises.tip: لَاصِق is 'sticking'; جُرُوح is 'wounds'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'I want something for allergies'?
exercises.tip: لِ before a noun means 'for'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'لِلْمَعِدَة؟ / هَلْ / شَيْءٌ / عِنْدَكُمْ'.
exercises.tip: The question word هَلْ always comes first.

phrases.arabic: هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَسَاسِيَّةٌ مِنْ أَيِّ دَوَاء؟

dialogue.speaker: Nasser
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. عِنْدِي مَوْعِدٌ مَعَ الطَّبِيب.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I have an appointment with the doctor.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Samir
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام. تَفَضَّلْ بِالْجُلُوس. مَاذَا يُؤْلِمُكَ؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. tafaddal bil-juloos. maadhaa yu2limuka?
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Please sit. What hurts you?

dialogue.speaker: Nasser
dialogue.english: My head hurts, and I have a fever.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Samir
dialogue.english: Since when have you been feeling this?

dialogue.speaker: Nasser
dialogue.english: For two days.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Samir
dialogue.arabic: خُذْ نَفَسًا عَمِيقًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. ضَغْطُ دَمِكَ مُرْتَفِعٌ قَلِيلًا.
dialogue.transliteration: khudh nafasan 3ameeqan, min fadlika. daghtu damika murtafi3un qaleelan.
dialogue.english: Take a deep breath, please. Your blood pressure is a bit high.

dialogue.speaker: Nasser
dialogue.english: Is it serious?

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Samir
dialogue.arabic: لَا، لَيْسَ الْأَمْرُ خَطِيرًا. هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَسَاسِيَّةٌ مِنْ أَيِّ دَوَاء؟
dialogue.transliteration: laa, laysa al-amru khateeran. hal 3indaka 7asaasiyyatun min ayyi dawaa2?
dialogue.english: No, it's nothing serious. Are you allergic to any medicine?

dialogue.speaker: Nasser
dialogue.english: No, I'm not.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Samir
dialogue.arabic: سَأَكْتُبُ لَكَ وَصْفَةً طِبِّيَّة، وَتَحْتَاجُ إِلَى الرَّاحَةِ لِعِدَّةِ أَيَّام.
dialogue.transliteration: sa-aktubu laka wasfatan tibbiyya, wa ta7taaju ilaa ar-raa7ati li-3iddati ayyaam.
dialogue.english: I'll write you a prescription, and you need to rest for a few days.

dialogue.speaker: Nasser
dialogue.english: When should I come back?

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Samir
dialogue.arabic: عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَعُودَ بَعْدَ أُسْبُوع. سَلَامَتُكَ، وَخُذْ رَاحَتَكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: 3alayka an ta3ooda ba3da usboo3. salaamatuka, wa khudh raa7ataka.
dialogue.english: You need to come back after a week. Get well soon, and take it easy.

dialogue.speaker: Nasser
dialogue.english: Thank you, doctor.

pair.english: Since when have you been feeling this?

pair.arabic: هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَسَاسِيَّةٌ مِنْ أَيِّ دَوَاء؟
pair.english: Are you allergic to any medicine?

lessons.culture: Doctors in the Arab world speak Fusha or a mix of Fusha and their dialect when they explain an illness, and the polite word to a patient is سَلَامَتُكَ. It is normal to be told to rest and to come back for a check after a week.

exercises.prompt: The doctor asks: 'مَاذَا يُؤْلِمُكَ؟'. Say that your head hurts.
exercises.tip: رَأْس is 'head'; the ending ي means 'my'.

exercises.prompt: The doctor asks: 'مُنْذُ مَتَى تَشْعُرُ بِهَذَا؟'. Say for two days.
exercises.tip: مُنْذُ answers 'since when' with a time.

exercises.prompt: The doctor asks: 'هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَسَاسِيَّةٌ مِنْ أَيِّ دَوَاء؟'. Say no.
exercises.tip: لَيْسَ عِنْدِي means 'I do not have'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'عِنْدِي _____ مَعَ الطَّبِيب.' (I have an appointment with the doctor.)
exercises.tip: مَوْعِد is an appointment or a fixed time.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'خُذْ _____ عَمِيقًا.' (Take a deep breath.)
exercises.tip: نَفَس is 'a breath'; عَمِيق is 'deep'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'You need to do some tests.'
exercises.tip: فُحُوصَات is 'tests' or 'examinations'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'I'll write you a prescription.' (to a man)
exercises.tip: سَ before the verb makes it future.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'It's nothing serious.'
exercises.tip: لَيْسَ makes the description negative: 'not serious'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Your blood pressure is a bit high'?
exercises.tip: ضَغْط الدَّم is 'blood pressure'; مُرْتَفِع is 'high'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'You need to come back after a week'?
exercises.tip: عَلَيْكَ أَنْ means 'you must'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'أَيَّام / لِعِدَّةِ / تَحْتَاجُ / إِلَى الرَّاحَةِ'.
exercises.tip: عِدَّة means 'several' and is followed by the plural.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Laila
dialogue.english: Where is the pain, Adam?

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.english: My back hurts, and also my neck.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Laila
dialogue.english: Does your head hurt?

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.english: A little. And I have a toothache.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Laila
dialogue.english: Show me your tooth, please.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.transliteration: haa hiya. wa rijlee mutawarrima aydan.
dialogue.english: Here it is. And my leg is swollen too.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Laila
dialogue.english: Since when?

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.english: Since yesterday. And my eye hurts a little.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Laila
dialogue.english: And your ear? Do you hear well?

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.arabic: نَعَمْ، أُذُنِي بِخَيْر، وَيَدِي بِخَيْر أَيْضًا.
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, udhunee bikhayr, wa yadee bikhayr aydan.
dialogue.english: Yes, my ear is fine, and my hand is fine too.

dialogue.speaker: Dr. Laila
dialogue.english: Then we'll check the back and the leg first.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.english: Thank you, doctor.

pair.english: What is wrong with your leg?

lessons.culture: Body parts are named with the article الـ in Fusha, and pain is usually said with the part first and the verb يُؤْلِمُنِي after it. Many Arabic body words are shared across every dialect, so this lesson is useful anywhere.

exercises.prompt: The doctor asks: 'أَيْنَ الْأَلَم؟'. Say that your back hurts.
exercises.tip: The body part comes first, then يُؤْلِمُنِي, 'hurts me'.

exercises.prompt: The doctor asks: 'هَلْ تَسْمَعُ جَيِّدًا؟'. Say yes, your ear is fine.
exercises.tip: بِخَيْر means 'fine' for a person or a body part.

exercises.prompt: The doctor asks: 'مَاذَا بِرِجْلِكَ؟'. Say that your leg is swollen.
exercises.tip: مُتَوَرِّمَة is 'swollen'; رِجْل is a feminine word.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'ظَهْرِي _____.' (My back hurts.)
exercises.tip: يُؤْلِمُنِي is 'hurts me'; a plural part uses يُؤْلِمَانِنِي or يُؤْلِمْنَنِي.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'عِنْدِي أَلَمٌ فِي _____.' (I have a toothache.)
exercises.tip: أَسْنَان is the plural of سِنّ, 'teeth'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I have a toothache.'
exercises.tip: أَلَم is 'pain'; فِي الْأَسْنَان is 'in the teeth'.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'My neck hurts.'
exercises.tip: رَقَبَة is feminine, so the verb starts with ت.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'My eye hurts a little.'
exercises.tip: قَلِيلًا at the end means 'a little'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'ear'?
exercises.tip: الْعَيْن is the eye and السِّنّ is the tooth.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'neck'?
exercises.tip: الظَّهْر is the back and الرَّأْس is the head.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'يُؤْلِمُنِي / ظَهْرِي / وَأَيْضًا / رَقَبَتِي'.
exercises.tip: وَأَيْضًا adds a second thing: 'and also'.

phrases.arabic: يُؤْلِمُنِي سِنِّي عِنْدَمَا أَشْرَبُ شَيْئًا بَارِدًا
سَأُعْطِيكَ حُقْنَةً حَتَّى لَا تَشْعُرَ بِأَلَم
أُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي بِالْفُرْشَاةِ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم
phrases.transliteration: unadhdhifu asnaanee bil-furshaati marratayni fee al-yawm

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: تَفَضَّلْ يَا عُمَر. أَيُّ سِنٍّ يُؤْلِمُكَ؟
dialogue.english: Please come in, Omar. Which tooth hurts you?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا السِّنّ. يُؤْلِمُنِي عِنْدَمَا أَشْرَبُ شَيْئًا بَارِدًا.
dialogue.transliteration: hadhaa as-sinn. yu2limunee 3indamaa ashrabu shay2an baaridan.
dialogue.english: This tooth. It hurts when I drink something cold.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: اِفْتَحْ فَمَكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. هَلْ يُؤْلِمُكَ هَذَا؟
dialogue.transliteration: iftah famaka min fadlika. hal yu2limuka hadhaa?
dialogue.english: Open your mouth please. Does this hurt you?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Yes, a little.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: لَدَيْكَ تَسَوُّسٌ فِي السِّنّ. سَنُجْرِي صُورَةً بِالْأَشِعَّة.
dialogue.transliteration: ladayka tasawwusun fee as-sinn. sa-nujree sooratan bil-ashi33a.
dialogue.english: You have a cavity. We'll take an X-ray.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Will the treatment hurt me?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: سَأُعْطِيكَ حُقْنَةً حَتَّى لَا تَشْعُرَ بِأَلَم.
dialogue.english: I'll give you an injection so you won't feel pain.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا يَا دُكْتُورَة. وَهَلْ أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى تَقْوِيمِ الْأَسْنَان؟
dialogue.transliteration: shukran yaa duktoora. wa hal a7taaju ilaa taqweemi al-asnaan?
dialogue.english: Thank you, doctor. And do I need braces?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: لَا، لَا تَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ. اِنْتَهَيْنَا. اِشْطِفْ فَمَكَ بِالْمَاء.
dialogue.transliteration: laa, laa ta7taaju ilayhi. intahaynaa. ishtif famaka bil-maa2.
dialogue.english: No, you don't need them. We're finished. Rinse your mouth with water.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: When can I eat?

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: Don't eat anything for two hours.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا لَكِ. سَأُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي بِالْفُرْشَاةِ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم.
dialogue.transliteration: shukran laki. sa-unadhdhifu asnaanee bil-furshaati marratayni fee al-yawm.
dialogue.english: Thank you. I'll brush my teeth twice a day.

lessons.culture: The dentist is called طَبِيبُ الْأَسْنَان, and a woman dentist is addressed as دُكْتُورَة. Many Muslims also clean their teeth with a سِوَاك, a small twig from the arak tree, which the Prophet (peace be upon him) encouraged. Brushing twice a day is the usual advice everywhere.

exercises.prompt: A dentist asks: 'أَيُّ سِنٍّ يُؤْلِمُكَ؟'. Say it is this tooth.
exercises.tip: هَذَا is 'this' for a masculine word like سِنّ.

exercises.prompt: The receptionist asks: 'هَلْ لَدَيْكَ مَوْعِد؟'. Say yes, at three.
exercises.tip: Hours are feminine, so the number is too: الثَّالِثَة.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'اِفْتَحْ _____ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.' (Open your mouth please.)
exercises.tip: فَم is 'mouth' and ـكَ means 'your' for a man.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'لَا تَأْكُلْ شَيْئًا لِمُدَّةِ _____.' (Don't eat anything for two hours.)
exercises.tip: Two of something ends with ـَيْنِ: سَاعَتَيْنِ.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I'll give you an injection so you won't feel pain.'
exercises.answer: سَأُعْطِيكَ حُقْنَةً حَتَّى لَا تَشْعُرَ بِأَلَم
accepted: سَأُعْطِيكَ حُقْنَةً حَتَّى لَا تَشْعُرَ بِأَلَم
ساعطيك حقنة حتى لا تشعر بالم
سَأُعْطِيكَ حُقْنَةً لِكَيْ لَا تَشْعُرَ بِالْأَلَم

too_formal.item: رَح أَعْطِيك إِبْرَة عَشَان مَا تُحِسّ بِوَجَع

exercises.tip: حَتَّى is followed by a verb ending with the vowel a: تَشْعُرَ.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Rinse your mouth with water.'
exercises.tip: اِشْطِفْ is the order 'rinse' to one man.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'You have a cavity'?
exercises.tip: تَسَوُّس is 'decay'; لَدَيْكَ means 'you have'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'My tooth hurts when I drink something cold'?
options: يُؤْلِمُنِي سِنِّي عِنْدَمَا أَشْرَبُ شَيْئًا بَارِدًا
أُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي بِالْفُرْشَاةِ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم
exercises.answer: يُؤْلِمُنِي سِنِّي عِنْدَمَا أَشْرَبُ شَيْئًا بَارِدًا
accepted: يُؤْلِمُنِي سِنِّي عِنْدَمَا أَشْرَبُ شَيْئًا بَارِدًا
يؤلمني سني عندما اشرب شيئا باردا
exercises.tip: عِنْدَمَا means 'when' and is followed by a verb.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'أَسْنَانِي / أُنَظِّفُ / مَرَّتَيْنِ / بِالْفُرْشَاةِ / فِي / الْيَوْم'.
exercises.answer: أُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي بِالْفُرْشَاةِ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم
accepted: أُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي بِالْفُرْشَاةِ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم
انظف اسناني بالفرشاة مرتين في اليوم
unadhdhifu asnaanee bil-furshaati marratayni fee al-yawm
exercises.tip: نَظَّفَ means 'to clean'; بِالْفُرْشَاةِ is 'with the brush'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'هَلْ / تَقْوِيمِ / أَحْتَاجُ / إِلَى / الْأَسْنَان'.
exercises.tip: اِحْتَاجَ إِلَى means 'to need'.

phrases.arabic: يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى الْبَقَاءِ فِي الْمُسْتَشْفَى يَوْمَيْن
phrases.transliteration: ya7taaju ilaa al-baqaa2i fee al-mustashfaa yawmayn

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.arabic: أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى مُسَاعَدَة. تَعَرَّضَ أَبِي لِحَادِث.
dialogue.transliteration: a7taaju ilaa musaa3ada. ta3arrada abee li-7aadith.
dialogue.english: I need help. My father had an accident.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: لَا تَقْلَقْ. سَجِّلْ اسْمَهُ عِنْدَ الِاسْتِقْبَال.
dialogue.english: Don't worry. Register his name at the reception desk.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.english: Where is the emergency room?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: فِي الطَّابِقِ الْأَرْضِيّ. سَأَقِيسُ حَرَارَتَهُ الْآن.
dialogue.english: On the ground floor. I'll measure his temperature now.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.english: I'm worried about him.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه، هُوَ بِخَيْرٍ الْآن. لَكِنَّهُ يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى الْبَقَاءِ فِي الْمُسْتَشْفَى يَوْمَيْن.
dialogue.transliteration: al-7amdu lillaah, huwa bi-khayrin al-aan. lakinnahu ya7taaju ilaa al-baqaa2i fee al-mustashfaa yawmayn.
dialogue.english: Praise be to Allah, he is fine now. But he needs to stay in the hospital for two days.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.english: Which room is he in?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.english: In room number five.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.english: What are the visiting hours?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.english: From four to six.

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.transliteration: wa mataa yumkinuhu al-khurooju mina al-mustashfaa?
dialogue.english: And when can he leave the hospital?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.english: Tomorrow, Allah willing.

pair.english: When can he leave the hospital?

lessons.culture: Visiting the sick is highly valued in Islam, so relatives and friends come to see a patient in person, and hospitals set visiting hours to keep the wards calm. People say شَفَاكَ اللَّه to a man and شَفَاكِ اللَّه to a woman, meaning 'may Allah heal you'. To someone who has recovered, they say الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه عَلَى السَّلَامَة.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'أَيْنَ قِسْمُ الطَّوَارِئ؟'. Say it is on the ground floor.
exercises.tip: الطَّابِق الْأَرْضِيّ is the 'ground floor', literally 'the earthly floor'.

exercises.prompt: A nurse is asked: 'مَا هِيَ مَوَاعِيدُ الزِّيَارَة؟'. Reply from four to six.
exercises.tip: Hours are feminine, so the numbers are too: الرَّابِعَة, السَّادِسَة.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى سَيَّارَةِ _____.' (I need an ambulance.)
exercises.tip: سَيَّارَةُ إِسْعَاف is literally 'a car of aid'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى الْبَقَاءِ فِي _____ يَوْمَيْن.' (He needs to stay in the hospital for two days.)
exercises.tip: الْمُسْتَشْفَى means 'hospital', from شِفَاء 'healing'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'My father had an accident.'
exercises.tip: تَعَرَّضَ لِ means 'to be hit by' something.

exercises.prompt: Translate: 'Praise be to Allah, he is fine now.'
exercises.tip: بِخَيْر means 'well'; Arabic needs no word for 'is'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'I'm worried about him'?
exercises.tip: قَلِق عَلَى means 'worried about'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Which room is he in?'
exercises.tip: أَيّ means 'which' and is followed by a noun.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'الْخُرُوجُ / يُمْكِنُهُ / مَتَى / مِنَ / الْمُسْتَشْفَى'.
exercises.tip: The question word مَتَى opens the sentence.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'سَجِّلْ / اسْمَهُ / عِنْدَ / الِاسْتِقْبَال'.
exercises.tip: ـهُ at the end of اسْمَهُ means 'his'.

challenge.title: At the pharmacy and the doctor
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha in which you feel unwell and go to a pharmacy. Say how you feel and for how long, ask for a medicine and its price, ask how to take it, and end with a wish of good health.
required_elements: a greeting and how you feel
a pain or illness with how long
the price and how often to take it
thanks and a wish of good health

dialogue.speaker: Ziad
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أَنَا مُتْعَب، وَعِنْدِي صُدَاع.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I'm tired, and I have a headache.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام. مُنْذُ مَتَى تَشْعُرُ بِهَذَا؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. mundhu mataa tash3uru bihaadhaa?
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Since when have you felt this?

dialogue.speaker: Ziad
dialogue.english: For two days. And I also have a fever.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: خُذْ هَذَا الدَّوَاءَ مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم.
dialogue.transliteration: khudh haadhaa ad-dawaa2a marratayni fee al-yawm.
dialogue.english: Take this medicine twice a day.

dialogue.speaker: Ziad
dialogue.english: Before eating or after?

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: بَعْدَ الْأَكْل. وَهُوَ يُسَبِّبُ النُّعَاسَ قَلِيلًا.
dialogue.transliteration: ba3da al-akl. wa huwa yusabbibu an-nu3aasa qaleelan.
dialogue.english: After eating. And it makes you a bit sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Ziad
dialogue.english: How much does it cost?

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: عَشَرَةُ دَنَانِير. وَإِنْ لَمْ تَتَحَسَّنْ، فَاذْهَبْ إِلَى الطَّبِيب.
dialogue.transliteration: 3asharatu danaaneer. wa in lam tata7assan, fadh-hab ilaa at-tabeeb.
dialogue.english: Ten dinars. And if you don't get better, go to the doctor.

dialogue.speaker: Ziad
dialogue.english: Alright. Thank you very much.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.english: You're welcome. Get well soon, and take it easy.
